title: Keyboard chord shortcuts + locale-aware feedback for compact cost widgets
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and validate a compact keyboard interaction model for Cost Explorer widgets that supports optional keyboard-chord shortcuts, ARIA announcements, and locale-aware feedback text. Goal is to improve discoverability for power users, keep single-key conflicts minimal, and ensure internationalized messages (number formats, plurals, RTL) are announced correctly by screen readers. Work covers prototypes, WCAG contrast checks for compact labels, and integration notes for engineering about debounce/burst typing when chords are held.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard chord flow documented and prototype in Figma with clear focus states
All dynamic announcements use ARIA-live with region politeness appropriate to context and avoid spurious repetition
Text and interactive label color contrast meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) for normal text and AAA guidance where feasible
Locale-aware message templates implemented and verified for en, fr, de, ja, ar with correct number grouping and pluralization
Edge conflict matrix created showing interactions with global app shortcuts and per-user remapping guidance
tasks: Finalize Figma prototype for compact cost card keyboard chords (primary + modifier combos)
Create aria-live pattern examples and copy variations for each supported locale
Run color token sweep and propose alternative tokens for low-contrast micro-labels
Coordinate with ENG to add aria attributes and a lightweight announcement debounce of 300ms
Accessibility QA: screen reader pass on Mac VoiceOver, NVDA/Windows, TalkBack/Android
Localization pass: export message keys, verify ICU-style plural rules and RTL rendering

decisions_made: Use two-step chord pattern (global prefix then action key) to reduce single-key conflicts
Implement 300ms announcement debounce and collapse repeated messages into a single summary
Adopt elevated secondary token for micro-labels and keep primary metrics at existing token
Expose chord remapping controls in Settings rather than per-widget to keep surface area minimal
